claims.text: A machine-learning-driven high-throughput screening framework using historical HEA data can rapidly identify promising RHEA compositions.
The identified RHEA compositions will have greater intrinsic strength than compositions designed by traditional thermo-kinetic or simulation methods.
The identified RHEA compositions will have greater ductility than compositions designed by traditional thermo-kinetic or simulation methods.
The identified RHEA compositions will have lower weight than compositions designed by traditional thermo-kinetic or simulation methods.
RHEAs occupy a broad multi-principal-element compositional space in which optimal compositions are undetermined.
A data-driven machine-learning model can predict property trends across the RHEA compositional space.
A data-driven machine-learning model can screen the RHEA compositional space rapidly.
Phase-stability indicators and interatomic-bonding characteristics are key compositional features underlying improved mechanical and weight properties in RHEAs.
Learning from historical data enables the model to uncover nonlinear relationships between composition and targeted mechanical properties.
The learned nonlinear relationships enable rapid selection of candidates likely to combine superior strength, ductility, and lower density.
Traditional thermo-kinetic and simulation-based composition design screens candidates more slowly and less efficiently than the proposed machine-learning approach.
The framework's predictive power depends on the historical training data being comprehensive and representative.
Underrepresentation of relevant compositional regions or physical phenomena can reduce the framework's predictive power.
Model-predicted RHEAs can be evaluated by synthesis followed by tensile testing and density measurement against traditionally designed control alloys.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement of at least 5% in mechanical performance or weight reduction relative to baseline alloys falsifies the hypothesis.
